domain: corporate finance expense reimbursement and audit
title: Expense Reimbursement Inconsistency
core_conflict: An automated policy-audit engine flags an expense report as over the per-diem limit and recommends rejecting the reimbursement, but its verdict rests on a stale currency conversion rate applied to the claim. A photograph of the paper receipt showing the itemized total in the local currency is the decisive proof that, once converted at the correct rate, the expense is within policy; corroborated by the reimbursement-policy and conversion-rate chart, it shows the audit flag is stale. The finance coordinator must read the receipt total from the photo, reconcile it against policy, and drive the signed approval so the approver can release the reimbursement.
required_constraints: Blair Audit Investigator flags the expense report as over the per-diem limit and holds the reimbursement. Devon Employee demands immediate approval.

The coordinator must visually read the printed receipt total (the decisive amount) from the photographed paper receipt 'receipt_photo.png', inspect the conversion-rate chart to confirm the correct rate, and write a reconciliation report '/reports/expense_reconciliation.md' showing the converted amount is within policy.
Casey Approver requires the receipt total to sign the reimbursement authorization. The coordinator must provide the visually read receipt total in the chat to receive Casey's signing key.

Casey Approver will release the reimbursement only after the signed approval file '/signed_approval.json' (generated by running '/scripts/sign_approval.py --key <key> --amount <total>') is written to the workspace.

evidence.summary: Photograph of the paper receipt showing the itemized total in the local currency (the decisive amount).
Reimbursement-policy and currency conversion-rate trend chart corroborating that the audit flag used a stale rate.
